name: Non-syndromic Unicoronal Craniosynostosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Unicoronal Craniosynostosis

criteria.description: Premature fusion of one coronal suture confirmed by imaging
Ipsilateral frontal bone flattening and contralateral frontal bossing
Ipsilateral orbital dystopia with elevation of the superior orbital rim
No clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic craniosynostosis
CT scan demonstrating suture fusion without additional sutural involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of premature unilateral coronal suture fusion with characteristic craniofacial asymmetry and absence of syndromic features confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on clinical examination and CT imaging; genetic testing may be used to exclude syndromic forms.

common.symptomName: Abnormal morphology of bony orbit of skull
searchTerms: abnormal shape of eye socket bones
skull bone changes around the eye

imaging: CT scan showing premature fusion of unilateral coronal suture
MRI to assess intracranial structures if neurological symptoms present
genetic: Absence of mutations in syndromic craniosynostosis genes (e.g., FGFR2, TWIST1) confirms non-syndromic status
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic craniofacial asymmetry
Neurodevelopmental assessment to monitor cognitive function

distinguishingFeatures: Associated limb anomalies or syndromic features
Genetic mutations in FGFR2, FGFR3, or TWIST1 genes
Head shape asymmetry due to external molding

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (persistent vomiting, severe headache)
references: Cohen MM Jr. Craniosynostosis: Diagnosis, Evaluation, and Management. 3rd ed. Oxford University Press; 2000.
Kimonis VE, Gold JA, Hoffman TL, Panchal J, Boyadjiev SA. Genetics of craniosynostosis. Semin Pediatr Neurol. 2007;14(3):150-161.
